layers.name: Can the radar see it? (surface change)
layers.attribution: Derived by CascadeLens from NISAR GUNW (NASA/ISRO) and Copernicus DEM GLO-30

keys.label: No valid data in the product

explanation.what: Could a surface change between these dates be seen here?
explanation.measures: Each spot gets its reasons kept separate: inside the frame or not, data present and unflagged by the product's own mask or not, hidden by terrain (layover or shadow, from the radar's own viewing angles and the elevation model), and signal quality. Missing inputs are marked Not assessed, never Usable.
explanation.inspect: Click any spot to see which reasons apply there. Grey and dark areas are not 'no change': they are places the radar could not judge.
explanation.establishes: Where a NISAR result can be trusted for this task. It does not say whether anything changed.

limitations: Only active layover and shadow from the local slope. Passive shadow cast by a distant ridge is not modelled, so some shadowed valleys may be marked visible.
The DEM is Copernicus GLO-30 resampled to the analysis grid; small features below the grid size are smoothed.
Coherence comes from the 80 m product, so features narrower than about 80 m are mixed with their surroundings.
Coherence also falls for reasons that are not surface change (wet snow, vegetation, a long time gap). The disturbance task only says whether a change could be seen, not whether one happened.
An exact zero in unwrapped phase is treated as unwrapping fill. A component's own reference pixel can be exactly zero, so at most one real pixel per component may be lost.
Products are Provisional.

layers.name: Landslide-prone terrain (screen)
layers.attribution: Derived by CascadeLens from Copernicus DEM GLO-30

explanation.what: Where the shape of the ground favours slope failure: steepness, converging hollows and wet ground.
explanation.measures: Slope, plan curvature and a topographic wetness index from the elevation model, combined by fixed, published rules.
explanation.inspect: Click a spot to see which terrain factors apply there.
explanation.establishes: A screen of terrain only. It is not a forecast, not trained on a Nepal landslide inventory, and leaves out geology, soil and rainfall.

limitations: Terrain only. Geology, soil, land cover, rainfall and earthquakes are not included, so this is a screen of where terrain favours failure, not a susceptibility map in the full sense.

Not trained or calibrated: no Nepal landslide inventory is loaded. The only check is a one-event consistency check against the UNOSAT 2026 detachment zone. It is not a validation: every unmapped pixel counts as a negative, and neighbouring pixels are not independent.
Not a forecast and not a warning. A high class does not mean a slope is about to fail.
Copernicus DEM GLO-30 resampled to 40 m; flow paths ignore pits and flats, and small gullies are smoothed.

explanation.measures: The difference of two gamma-0 VV backscatter values, in decibels.

explanation.establishes: Change in how the surface returned the radar. It does not establish the cause, and it is a different mission from NISAR.

limitations: Sentinel-1 is an ESA mission; NASA's OPERA project made these terrain-corrected images from it. Not a NISAR result.
Both dates are before 26 August: this is the control for ordinary 12-day change.
Layover and shadow pixels flagged by OPERA are left out.
C-band reacts to soil moisture and vegetation more than NISAR's L-band.

layers.attribution: Derived by CascadeLens from NASA/JPL OPERA RTC-S1 (from Copernicus Sentinel-1 data, ESA); distributed by ASF DAAC

explanation.what: How much brighter or darker Sentinel-1 saw each spot on 5 September 2026 than on 24 August 2026, from NASA's OPERA terrain-corrected images of one orbit track.
explanation.measures: The difference of two gamma-0 VV backscatter values, in decibels.
explanation.inspect: Compare the pair across the event with the 12-day pair before it, inside and outside the mapped mudflow.
explanation.establishes: Change in how the surface returned the radar. It does not establish the cause, and it is a different mission from NISAR.

limitations: Sentinel-1 is an ESA mission; NASA's OPERA project made these terrain-corrected images from it. Not a NISAR result.
The 26 August event falls between the two dates, and so does 12 days of monsoon weather.
Layover and shadow pixels flagged by OPERA are left out.
C-band reacts to soil moisture and vegetation more than NISAR's L-band.

layers.unitsNote: 28 August 2026 minus 16 August 2026, VV, in dB, from 80 m averages of the linear gamma-0 terms.

layers.instrument: OpenStreetMap roads + terrain screen + Radar Observability
layers.name: Road exposure (screen)
layers.attribution: Derived by CascadeLens from OpenStreetMap (ODbL), Copernicus DEM, UNOSAT and NISAR GUNW
limitations: A screen, not a risk rating: traffic, road design, retaining walls and drainage are unknown.
OpenStreetMap roads exported after the event; some may have moved or closed.
Click a road segment to see why it is rated as it is, and whether the radar can watch it.

layers.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, NISAR; distributed by ASF DAAC
layers.name: Coherence through time (Track 98, frame 16)

explanation.what: Coherence of every catalogued Track 98 frame 16 pair, one time step per pair, from 2026-07-26 to 2026-10-06.
explanation.measures: How alike the radar echoes stayed between the two dates of each pair, 0 to 1, on the unwrapped grid, with the product's own mask applied.
explanation.inspect: Click a spot and open the Inspector: the chart shows that spot in each pair. Play the steps under Simulate, Time replay.
explanation.establishes: Whether a spot stayed coherent before, across and after the event. It does not say what changed, or measure movement.

limitations: Pairs are not alike: lengths 12, 24 days and radar modes 4000 in the file names. Longer pairs and different modes lower coherence by themselves.
One value per pair, nothing interpolated between pairs.
Provisional data.

disturbance.label: Usable
disturbance.meaning: The radar saw this ground clearly before and across the event, so a change here would show.

disturbance.label: Seen, but not reliable
disturbance.meaning: The ground was already incoherent in the baseline pair, so a drop across the event cannot be told apart from normal noise.

disturbance.meaning: Outside the radar frame assessed here. A neighbouring frame or another track may cover it, but it is not checked yet: no conclusion, not no change.

coherenceMin.provenance: Project choice. 0.3 is a common lower bound for usable L-band phase; results at 0.2 and 0.4 are reported alongside so the choice can be checked.

layover.value: range slope toward the radar > incidence angle
layover.provenance: Standard SAR geometry (layover occurs when the terrain slope facing the sensor exceeds the incidence angle).

shadow.value: range slope away from the radar > 90 deg - incidence angle

coherenceProduct.value: unwrappedInterferogram coherenceMagnitude, 80 m, sampled nearest onto the 40 m grid
coherenceProduct.provenance: The coherence that belongs to the unwrapped phase and shares its mask; the same layer the app shows.

sensitivity.denominator: All analysis cells inside the frame footprint, over the whole case area.
sensitivity.rule: The same rule as the movement class, with only the coherence threshold changed.

limitations: Only active layover and shadow from the local slope. Passive shadow cast by a distant ridge is not modelled, so some shadowed valleys may be marked visible.
The DEM is Copernicus GLO-30 resampled to the analysis grid; small features below the grid size are smoothed.
Coherence comes from the 80 m product, so features narrower than about 80 m are mixed with their surroundings.
Coherence also falls for reasons that are not surface change (wet snow, vegetation, a long time gap). The disturbance task only says whether a change could be seen, not whether one happened.
An exact zero in unwrapped phase is treated as unwrapping fill. A component's own reference pixel can be exactly zero, so at most one real pixel per component may be lost.
Products are Provisional.

controlSeries.ciMethod: Spatial block bootstrap of the median: 1000 m blocks, 1000 resamples, seed 0

classes.label: Low
classes.meaning: Gentle ground (under 15 deg), or moderate slopes with no other factor.

classes.label: Moderate
classes.meaning: Moderately steep, or steep but neither convergent nor wet.

classes.label: High
classes.meaning: Steep and either convergent or wet.

classes.label: Very high
classes.meaning: 35 deg or steeper, convergent and wet: where shallow slides and debris flows typically start.

slopeBandsDeg.provenance: Project choice of common slope classes; they are not calibrated for Nepal. Each band's share of the mapped 2026 detachment zone is reported so the choice can be checked.

wet.value: TWI above the 75th percentile of slopes over 15 deg
wet.provenance: Relative, project choice. TWI = ln(a / tan b) with D8 flow accumulation (Beven and Kirkby 1979).

validation.kind: One-event consistency check, not a validation
caveats: One event only: the UNOSAT 2026 detachment zone.
Every unmapped pixel is treated as a confirmed negative, which it is not.
Neighbouring pixels are not independent, so the AUC has no meaningful sample size.
Pixels with no valid elevation (class 0) are left out.

mudflowRunout.note: The runout is where debris travelled and settled, mostly valley floors. A terrain screen for slope failure is not expected to rank it high.

limitations: Terrain only. Geology, soil, land cover, rainfall and earthquakes are not included, so this is a screen of where terrain favours failure, not a susceptibility map in the full sense.

Not trained or calibrated: no Nepal landslide inventory is loaded. The only check is a one-event consistency check against the UNOSAT 2026 detachment zone. It is not a validation: every unmapped pixel counts as a negative, and neighbouring pixels are not independent.
Not a forecast and not a warning. A high class does not mean a slope is about to fail.
Copernicus DEM GLO-30 resampled to 40 m; flow paths ignore pits and flats, and small gullies are smoothed.

rules.High: Crosses ground mapped as hit in 2026, or 30% or more of the ground within 150 m screens High or Very high
rules.Moderate: 10% or more screens High or Very high, or within 100 m of a mapped river (OpenStreetMap)
rules.radarWatch: Share of the 150 m corridor where the event pair could see a surface change: 50% or more = can watch, 20 to 50% = partly, under 20% = cannot
rules.radarWatchEither: The same rule on the share usable from either the main view or view t98; the two views are never merged into one reason

needs: GPM IMERG daily rainfall for Aug 2026

screen.name: Also close every stretch on ground mapped as hit

limitations: A screen, not a statement about who can be reached: footpaths, river crossings, unmapped tracks and helicopters are outside this network.
The network stops at the study area. A detour that leaves it, for example through Kathmandu, is not found, so 'no road path in this network' can be a boundary effect.
Only facilities mapped in OSM inside the study area are destinations: three here. Others, including those just outside, are not counted.
'No path in either' means the mapped roads do not join even with every road open: a gap in the mapping or the network, not a closure.
OpenStreetMap is incomplete and was edited after the event; roads may be missing or out of date.
A road with no report is Unknown. The reported network leaves it open, which may be wrong either way.
No traffic, road condition, vehicle type or season is modelled; distances are along the mapped centre line.
